text.content:
Status is the measure of a vampire's reputation among her own kind, recorded in Traits. It usually stems from holding office (prince, primogen, scourge, and so on), but can also be gained through influence, extraordinary deeds, or simply being noticed by the right people at the right time. Status only matters within the sect that granted it — Camarilla and Sabbat Status do not transfer, since the sects hold each other in such contempt that one sect's reputation carries no weight with the other.

Camarilla Status Traits

Acknowledged, Admired, Adored, Cherished, Esteemed, Exalted, Famous, Faultless, Feared, Honorable, Influential, Just, Praised, Respected, Revered, Trustworthy, Well-Connected, Well-Known.

All vampires officially "accepted" by the prince acquire the Status Trait Acknowledged. Without it, a character can't expect even simple favors from local Kindred, and may be hunted by the scourge if discovered. Most characters start with this Trait or acquire it early in the chronicle.

Troupes are encouraged to invent new Status Traits to suit their own stories.

Using Status

Status comes in two forms:

  • Permanent Status is recorded on the character sheet and reflects actual standing; permanent gains and losses are added or removed from the sheet directly.
  • Temporary Status fluctuates more freely and has no effect on permanent Status. It's often represented with Status Cards since it changes hands frequently.

A Status Trait may be bid instead of a regular Trait in any applicable Social Challenge, or added to your Social Traits when totals are compared at a tie. You must announce that you're using Status this way; an opponent may choose to ignore it (a disrespectful act that typically costs the offender permanent Status, unless the ignored Kindred was far less influential).

Troupes are encouraged to assign a Narrator (the "Gossip") to keep written records of Status-relevant events like loans, boons, and snubs.

Other Uses

  • Temporary Status may add to Social Traits in an applicable Social Challenge (not for Discipline use unless the Storyteller approves).
  • Status measures credibility: when it's one vampire's word against another's, or an accusation lacks hard evidence, the character with more Status is believed.
  • Status may be loaned: the lender's temporary Status Trait can be used by the borrower as her own for the rest of the story, but must be returned immediately on request. This is the only way temporary Status can exceed permanent Status. A character may loan only one Trait of Status to any one person at a time.
  • A character needs at least one Status Trait to petition the prince for any reason.
  • Anyone of higher Status may strip permanent Status from someone lower, at a cost of one of their own permanent Status Traits per Trait removed (temporary Status may be removed the same way).
  • A character may grant permanent Status to a clanmate who has less than half her own permanent Status, at a cost of one temporary Status Trait, made publicly (e.g. at a primogen meeting).
  • A clan may collectively remove one Status Trait from an elder of the clan by spending a group total of permanent Status equal to the elder's permanent Status; the primogen may lower the prince's Status the same way.

Gaining and Losing Status

A character may gain only one Status Trait per story (exceptions: Status granted/sanctioned by the prince, or Status received for assuming a station). A character can lose more than one Status Trait per story. Common ways to gain Status: upholding the Traditions (especially the Masquerade), favors for the prince or an elder, saving a prominent Kindred's unlife, or defeating a Sabbat threat. Common ways to lose it: false accusations, violating the Traditions, diablerie, or refusing to recognize another Kindred's Status.

Stations

Eight standard stations grant Status within a city; small cities may double up roles or leave some vacant. All powers a station grants are lost immediately on leaving the post.

  • The Prince: Gains Exalted, Well-Known, and Famous (cannot be permanently lost while prince). May remove one permanent Status Trait from anyone at a cost of one temporary Trait, and may grant permanent Status at a cost of one temporary Trait per Trait awarded — the prince alone may exceed the one-Trait-per-story limit this way (granting more than three in one session costs the prince permanent Status for the fourth Trait onward). The first Status Trait (Acknowledged) costs the prince nothing to grant a newly Presented neonate.
  • Seneschal: Gains Cherished and Esteemed. Acts with full princely authority while the prince is away (reversible by the prince at any time).
  • Primogen: Each member gains Revered while serving. May grant or remove permanent Status to/from clanmates at a cost of one temporary Trait per Trait.
  • Harpies: The leader gains Influential. Receives one temporary Status Trait from each primogen member automatically, usable however she likes. May remove one permanent Status Trait (at no cost) from a Kindred caught reneging on a boon or embroiled in a real scandal, with evidence presented publicly; may restore Status she removed at a cost of one temporary Trait per Trait. May sponsor lesser harpies by gifting them a Status Trait of her own.
  • Whips: Hold the same powers as primogen but gain no extra Status Trait, and their authority can be revoked at any time by their clan's primogen.
  • Sheriff: Gains Feared. May summon any Kindred in the city for questioning or judgment; refusal costs the offender one permanent Status Trait. Immune to the keeper of Elysium's positional powers (though still bound by the Traditions). May sponsor deputies with the sheriff's own powers, revocable at any time.
  • Keeper of Elysium: Gains Honorable. May remove one permanent Status Trait at no cost from any Kindred caught (or sufficiently evidenced) breaking the Masquerade.
  • Scourge: Gains Feared. May harass, detain, or destroy without penalty any vampire Embraced without permission or never formally Presented to the prince. May strip a permanent Status Trait at no cost from anyone caught harboring such a vampire, with evidence presented to the prince (who may overturn an unconvincing case). Not every city maintains this office, and even those that do rarely see it as a noble calling.

Prestation (Boons)

Prestation is the formal system of favors and debts among Kindred. When one vampire does a favor for another, the receiver owes a boon, categorized as trivial, minor, major, blood, or life. The parties agree on a number of Status (or Influence) Traits the receiver gives the bestower as Boon Traits, plus any conditions (most commonly: "You may not take physical action against me for the duration of this boon").

  • Trivial boon (roughly one Trait): a one-time favor, like protecting someone for an evening or supporting a political move.
  • Minor boon (two Traits): lasts more than one evening and involves some inconvenience — safe passage, sharing crucial information, removing a minor threat.
  • Major boon (three Traits): a large expenditure of time or resources with lasting effect, such as teaching a Discipline or buying someone a haven.
  • Blood boon (four Traits): the bestower risked her own safety to help the receiver.
  • Life boon (five Traits): the bestower risked her unlife outright for the receiver.

Boon Traits behave like loaned Status, except the bestower's loss is only temporary (restored at the start of the next story), and the original owner cannot demand the Traits back early — only repayment of the boon returns them. The only ways to permanently shed a boon are to repay it or to ignore it outright; ignoring a major, blood, or life boon always costs the receiver Status and risks the bestower's anger.

Camarilla Justice

The prince typically administers city justice; most infractions of the Traditions carry death or exile, though some princes substitute a blood bond to themselves or the primogen. Only the primogen council can reverse a prince's ruling, and only by collectively spending temporary Status equal to the prince's permanent Status (failure costs each primogen member an additional Status Trait). The prince may call a blood hunt, obligating every Kindred in the city to help track down and destroy the guilty party.

Justicars are the Camarilla's true cross-city authority: one per member clan, elected for 13-year terms, answering only to the Inner Circle, overrulable only by another justicar. A justicar may call a conclave, open to all Camarilla vampires in the area; a Kindred sentenced there may appeal only by requesting an ordeal — a demanding, time-limited quest where failure means death. Justicars often send archons as representatives ahead of their own arrival; hosting cities are advised to cooperate quickly.

Sabbat Status Traits

Battle-Scarred, Blessed, Blooded, Confirmed, Devoted, Enlightened, Enriched, Feared, Hunted, Infamous, Initiated, Loyal, Ominous, Proven, Respected, Undefeated.

Sabbat Status reflects different values than Camarilla Status and functions only within the sect. Vampires who haven't yet earned Initiated cannot hold or gain any Sabbat Status at all.

Sabbat Hierarchy

The Regent leads the sect, advised by prisci (singular: priscus) and cardinals. Archbishops control individual cities; within a city, bishops function much like primogen. Paladins/templars serve as bodyguards and enforcers (barred from the Black Hand, but formidable regardless). Within a pack: the pack leader commands and inspires, the pack priest leads rituals and ensures rites are observed, and the abbot oversees the communal haven's safety and day-to-day matters.

Gaining and Losing Sabbat Status

Sabbat Status changes mostly through pack consensus or directives from higher rank. A pack can scratch off a member's Trait by unanimous agreement; Traits earned by the whole pack (like Blooded) can't be removed except by the same collective process, while individually-perceived Traits (like Proven) can be revoked more easily. Higher-ranked, higher-Status Sabbat may also remove Traits directly, though packs are fiercely loyal to their leaders and may mutiny rather than accept a Status strip.

To award Status: an individual needs at least five permanent Status Traits of her own; a pack acting collectively needs a group total of at least seven. Each pack member spending Status toward the award contributes one Trait, and for every two Traits spent the honoree gains one Status Trait, capped at three new Traits gained per occasion.
